@jmartisk could it be that when you have a gauge, the bean is instantiated later and thus might need the constructor to be included in the native image?
Perhaps we just need to register the bean for reflection when `@Gauge` is used?

Including a `@Gauge` does not change when the bean is instantiated I think, it's still a regular `ApplicationScoped` bean, we just attach `@MetricsBinding`, which binds to it an interceptor that intercepts the bean's constructor (via `@AroundConstruct`)

Sorry, I just saw the full error. Maybe we should just register `InMemoryStorageService` for reflection? Well just it's constructors I guess. That would probably be the easiest way to go, although I highly suspect we can get around that.

I can take a look if you like.

@geoand You could read the config at build time (if that's an option here) and then generate [synthetic bean](https://quarkus.io/guides/cdi-reference#synthetic-beans) or register [additional bean](https://quarkus.io/guides/cdi-reference#additional-beans). Something like that?

@manovotn I was basically asking what a user could do.
The pattern that is being used in this application seems common but I would really like to make it easier somehow for a user to choose the implementation (I guess based on some config value)
Well, in a way it is similar to those Spring-like profiles we were talking recently. On the same principle you could apply this.

I woke up thinking exactly that 😂. 
I believe it's something we should consider adding
